name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
scope_notes: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

controls.name: Restrict personal access tokens (classic) from accessing your organizations
controls.what: Blocks classic PATs from org-owned resources; public resources stay reachable.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Tokens (classic) tab
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens (classic) or fine-grained personal access tokens cannot access resources owned by the organization. SSH keys created by personal access tokens will continue to work.

controls.name: Fine-grained personal access tokens (restrict access)
controls.what: Blocks fine-grained PATs from org-owned resources.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Fine-grained tokens tab
controls.quote: By default, both Personal access tokens (classic) and fine-grained personal access tokens are enabled.

controls.name: Restrict access via personal access tokens (enterprise policy)
controls.what: Enterprise owners block classic and/or fine-grained PATs from all enterprise orgs; orgs cannot override.
controls.setting: Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens cannot access organizations owned by the enterprise. SSH keys created by these personal access tokens will continue to work. Organizations cannot override this setting.

controls.name: Require approval of fine-grained personal access tokens
controls.what: An org owner must approve each fine-grained PAT before it can access org resources (owner-created tokens exempt).
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Fine-grained tokens; enterprise policy can force on/off
controls.quote: Require administrator approval: An organization owner must approve each fine-grained personal access token that can access the organization. Fine-grained personal access tokens created by organization owners will not need approval. This is the default value.

controls.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
controls.what: Blocks member PATs whose lifetime exceeds the limit from org resources; tokens are not revoked. Enterprise can set a ceiling.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings (per token type); Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: For fine-grained personal access tokens, the default the maximum lifetime policy for organizations is set to expire within 366 days. Personal access tokens (classic) do not have an expiration requirement.

controls.name: Require SAML SSO authentication for all members
controls.what: Members must authenticate via the IdP; classic PATs and SSH keys must be SSO-authorized, and OAuth/GitHub App user authorizations need an active SSO session.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > SAML single sign-on; or enterprise-level SAML
controls.quote: You must authorize your personal access token (classic) after creation before the token can access an organization that uses SAML single sign-on (SSO).

controls.name: Revoke SSO authorizations / Delete keys and tokens
controls.what: Owners revoke SSO authorizations (SAML) or delete credentials (EMU only) per user, per credential type, or in bulk.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security; enterprise incident response; REST API
controls.plan: GitHub Enterprise Cloud (SAML SSO or EMU)
controls.quote: Revoking authorizations removes SSO authorizations for user tokens and SSH keys, either for a specific user, all users, or a specific credential type, across all organizations in your enterprise.

controls.name: Review and revoke fine-grained personal access tokens
controls.what: Org owners view and revoke any fine-grained PAT's access to the org.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Active tokens; REST API (GitHub Apps only)
controls.quote: Organization owners can view all fine-grained personal access tokens that can access resources owned by the organization. Organization owners can also revoke access by fine-grained personal access tokens.

controls.name: IP allow list
controls.what: Blocks PATs, OAuth app tokens, SSH/deploy keys, GitHub App tokens and GITHUB_TOKEN from non-allowed IPs (not user-installed apps' installation tokens).
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list; Enterprise settings > Authentication security
controls.quote: IP allow lists don't currently restrict access when a GitHub App is installed on a user account and uses server-to-server installation tokens to access an organization or enterprise.

controls.name: Enable IP allow list configuration for installed GitHub Apps
controls.what: Adds IPs declared by installed GitHub Apps to the org allow list so app requests from those IPs are permitted.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list
controls.quote: If you select Enable IP allow list configuration for installed GitHub Apps in your allow list settings, then IP addresses from installed GitHub Apps are added to your allow list.

controls.name: OAuth app access restrictions
controls.what: Unapproved OAuth apps cannot access private org resources; members must request owner approval.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy
controls.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources. Users can request owner approval for OAuth apps they'd like to use

controls.name: Deny access to a previously approved OAuth app
controls.what: Owners remove an approved OAuth app's access to the org.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy
controls.quote: At the organization level, deny the app access. At the user level, revoke the app authorization and its associated tokens.

controls.name: App access requests
controls.what: Controls whether members/outside collaborators may request installation or approval of unapproved apps.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access
controls.quote: By default, app access requests are enabled. If your organization has a large number of members or outside collaborators, you may want to disable app access requests to reduce the number of requests you have to review.

controls.name: Restrict GitHub App installation to organization owners
controls.what: Repository admins cannot install GitHub Apps or add repos to existing installations; they must request it.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access
controls.quote: As an organization owner, you can restrict GitHub App installations to only organization owners.

controls.name: GitHub App installation repository access
controls.what: Owners limit an installed app to all or selected repositories.
controls.setting: Org settings > GitHub Apps > Configure > Repository access
controls.quote: Organization owners can change the repository access for an app installed on their organization.

controls.name: Suspend / Uninstall GitHub App
controls.what: Temporarily or permanently blocks an installed app from org resources.
controls.setting: Org settings > GitHub Apps > Configure > Suspend or Uninstall; enterprise owners also
controls.quote: You can also temporarily or permanently prevent a GitHub App from accessing resources owned by your account or organization.

controls.name: Workflow permissions (default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions)
controls.what: Sets the default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only contents/packages or read/write; workflows can still change it via the permissions key.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: Under "Workflow permissions", choose whether you want the GITHUB_TOKEN to have read and write access for all permissions (the permissive setting), or just read access for the contents and packages permissions (the restricted setting).

controls.name: Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests
controls.what: When off, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot create or approve pull requests.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: By default, when you create a new organization, workflows are not allowed to create or approve pull requests.

controls.name: Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests (fork PRs)
controls.what: Controls whether fork pull-request workflows get a write GITHUB_TOKEN; otherwise it is read-only.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Fork pull request workflows
controls.quote: Run workflows from fork pull requests. Users can run workflows from fork pull requests. By default, workflows will use a GITHUB_TOKEN with read-only permission, with no access to secrets.

controls.name: Actions policies (disable GitHub Actions)
controls.what: Disabling Actions for all or selected repositories prevents workflows (and their GITHUB_TOKEN) from running.
controls.setting: Org settings > Actions > General > Policies; enterprise policy can override
controls.quote: You can choose to disable GitHub Actions for all repositories in your organization, or only allow specific repositories.

controls.name: Deploy keys (allow/disallow creation)
controls.what: Disallowing deploy keys blocks creation and disables existing deploy keys in all org repos.
controls.setting: Org settings > Repository > Deploy keys; Enterprise settings > Policies > Repository > Deploy keys
controls.quote: By default, new organizations are configured to disallow the creation of deploy keys in repositories.

controls.name: Enforcing a policy for deploy keys (enterprise)
controls.what: Enterprise owners allow, restrict, or delegate deploy key creation for all orgs; disabling disables existing keys.
controls.setting: Enterprise settings > Policies > Repository > Deploy keys
controls.quote: Changing this setting to disabled will result in existing deploy keys being disabled in all repositories in the enterprise.

no_control.what: Classic PATs cannot be put under an approval workflow; only fine-grained PATs can.
no_control.quote: Only fine-grained personal access tokens, not personal access tokens (classic), are subject to approval.

no_control.what: Enterprise revoke/delete credential actions do not cover GitHub App installation tokens, deploy keys or GITHUB_TOKEN.
no_control.quote: The following credential types are not affected by either action: GitHub App installation tokens (ghs_) Deploy keys GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN access

no_control.what: Admins cannot stop repo writers from raising GITHUB_TOKEN permissions in the workflow file above the default.
no_control.quote: Anyone with write access to a repository can modify the permissions granted to the GITHUB_TOKEN, adding or removing access as required, by editing the permissions key in the workflow file.

no_control.what: GitHub Apps are not subject to the OAuth app access policy.
no_control.quote: GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies. A GitHub App only has access to the repositories an organization owner has granted.

controls_unknown: Whether admins can set a maximum lifetime for GitHub App user access tokens or OAuth app tokens (only app-developer settings found).
Whether GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permission defaults can be made non-overridable.

authentication.summary: A classic OAuth app gets a gho_ user access token through the web or device flow and sends it as Authorization: Bearer. The token acts as the user, limited by the granted scopes.

federation.details: The token is obtained by user authorization in the web or device flow. SAML/OIDC SSO authorization is granted automatically during an active SSO session, but no inbound token exchange is documented for this path.

ip_restriction.boundary: The organization/enterprise IP allow list (Enterprise Cloud only) covers OAuth app tokens. Unlike GitHub Apps, OAuth app IPs cannot be added automatically. With the IdP (Entra OIDC CAP) allow list, GitHub sends the app server's IP for validation, and admins can exempt authorized OAuth apps.

lifetime.summary: Long-lived; revoked after 1 year unused. App can opt in to 8-hour expiring tokens

renewal.summary: By default the same token is reused until revoked or unused for one year. If the app requires expiring tokens or requests offline_access, a refresh token (expires after six months unused) issues a new 8-hour token.

administration.summary: Users revoke an app's authorization in their settings. Organization owners control access with OAuth app access restrictions (on by default for new orgs) and can deny a previously approved app. Anyone holding a leaked token value can revoke it through the API. GitHub keeps at most ten tokens per user/app/scope.
administration.conditions: IP allow lists and SAML SSO need Enterprise Cloud. Admins cannot revoke SSO authorization for individual OAuth app tokens, and these authorizations are not visible in the UI.

sso.details: OAuth app tokens get SSO authorization automatically only during an active SAML/OIDC session; CAP checks the app server IP for user-context requests.

offboard.details: Offboarded users' app authorizations can no longer be used against enterprise/org resources.

authentication.summary: An SSH key pair whose public key is attached to a single repository; the private key stays on the server and authenticates Git operations over SSH. Keys are read-only by default, and write access can be granted when the key is added.

federation.details: Static SSH key registered on the repository; no external identity exchange is involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: An organization or enterprise IP allow list (GitHub Enterprise Cloud only) covers SSH keys, including deploy keys, for organization-owned repositories. IdP conditional access policy (CAP) IP conditions, used with OIDC for Enterprise Managed Users, do not apply to deploy keys because they do not act on behalf of a user.

lifetime.summary: No expiry; valid until deleted or disabled

renewal.summary: The same key is reused until a repository admin deletes it or deploy keys are disabled by policy; removing the user who added it does not deactivate it.

administration.summary: Added in repository settings by someone with access to them, or through the REST API (fine-grained tokens need repository Administration write). Organization owners can disable deploy key creation, and enterprise owners can set the policy for all organizations; disabling the setting also disables existing deploy keys. Additions and removals are logged as public_key.create and public_key.delete audit events.
administration.conditions: One key per repository; a key can't be reused across repositories. New organizations disallow deploy key creation by default. A write-enabled key can do what an organization member with admin access can do on that repository. A key created through the API with a personal access token or OAuth app token is deleted when that token is deleted or revoked; keys created with GitHub App tokens are not. Keys are not tied to organization membership.

sso.details: Deploy keys are repository-scoped, are not SSO-authorized, and IdP CAP IP conditions do not apply to them.

offboard.details: Deploy keys are tied to the repository; they stay active when the creating user is removed.

inventory.details: Only per repository via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys or repo settings; deploy keys are not in the enterprise credential inventory types.
